match.reason: None of the bank points teaches choosing between confusable endings like -tion/-sion, -ance/-ence or -able/-ible; the closest, Spelling strategies for new words, covers general strategies and suffixes more broadly, so a new point is needed.

draft.title: Common endings in academic words
card: -tion
This is the most common ending for nouns, such as education and equation. It often follows a verb that ends in -ate or -ect, such as create and creation.
-sion
It is used after a stem ending in d, s or r, as in decision, expansion and conversion. Use the verb to check: decide gives decision.
-able and -ible
-able often joins a whole word, such as adapt and adaptable. -ible often joins a stem that is not a word alone, such as visible and flexible.
-ance and -ence
Match the family: -ance goes with words like tolerance and importance, -ence with words like evidence and science. No rule covers all cases, so learn the word.
draft.remember: Use the verb or the word family to choose the ending, and learn the exceptions.

a.q: Which spelling of this science word is correct?
opts: evaporation
evaporasion
evaporatian
evaporacion
a.why: The verb evaporate leads to evaporation, with -tion after -ate. The -sion ending is used after d, s or r, so it does not fit here.

b.q: A Year 8 science report says a metal is adapt___ to hot places. Which choice is correct, and why?
opts: adaptable, because adapt is a whole word
adaptible, because adapt is a whole word
adaptable, because the stem is not a word
adaptible, because the stem is not a word
b.why: Adapt is a whole word, so -able is added to it. The -ible choice would suit a stem that cannot stand alone, such as vis in visible.
b.clue: Can adapt stand alone as a word?

b.best: adaptable, because adapt is a whole word

problems.detail: Flexible is given as an -ible word whose stem is not a word alone, but flex is a whole word. The example clashes with the rule it is meant to show; use a word such as edible, audible or legible instead.

The -sion rule is wrong as stated. Conversion comes from convert, which ends in t, not d, s or r. Many -tion words also follow r or s, such as assertion, portion and suggestion, so 'it is used after a stem ending in d, s or r' misleads. Use verbs ending in -d/-de (decide, expand) or -se/-mit (revise, permit), and say 'often'.
The why repeats the faulty rule that -sion 'is used after d, s or r'. This reinforces an overstated rule that many -tion words break.
'-tion: This is the most common ending for nouns' overstates. It is the most common of these similar-sounding endings, not of all noun endings.

proposal.title: Common endings in academic words
card: -tion
This is the most common of these sound-alike endings, as in education and equation. It often follows a verb ending in -ate or -ect, such as create and creation.
-sion
Verbs ending in -d or -de often take -sion, as in expand and expansion, or decide and decision. So do many ending in -se or -mit, as in revise and revision, or permit and permission.
-able and -ible
-able often joins a whole word, such as adapt and adaptable. -ible often joins a stem that is not a word alone, such as visible and edible.
-ance and -ence
No firm rule covers these, so learn each word. A related -ant or -ent word can help: important gives importance, and evident gives evidence.
